Q1666164.label: 1926 Canadian federal election
Q1666164.summary: The 1926 Canadian federal election was held on September 14, 1926, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada of the 16th Parliament of Canada. The election was called after an event known as the King–Byng affair.

Q3587188.label: 2002 Jamaican general election
Q3587188.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 16 October 2002. The result was a victory for the People's National Party, which won 34 of the 60 seats, whilst voter turnout was 59%. PNP leader P. J. Patterson retained his position as Prime Minister, becoming the first political leader to win three successive elections.

Q365172.label: Carlos Arias Navarro
Q365172.summary: Carlos Arias Navarro, 1st Marquess of Arias Navarro, was a Spanish politician who was the Prime Minister of Spain from 1973 to 1976, serving during the final years of the Francoist era and the beginning of the country's transition to democracy.

Q55924.desc: Polish politician, Prime Minister of Poland (1946-2015)
Q55924.summary: Józef Oleksy was a Polish left-wing politician who served as Prime Minister of Poland from 7 March 1995 to 7 February 1996, when he resigned due to espionage allegations. He was chairman of the Democratic Left Alliance.

Q7541876.label: Slovenian regionalisation referendum, 2008
Q7541876.summary: A referendum on establishing thirteen provinces was held in Slovenia on 22 June 2008. While turnout was only 10.9% of registered voters, voters in all but two of the thirteen proposed provinces approved the change, the exception being the Central Slovenia and Coastal–Karst provinces.

Q3566196.label: 1976 Cypriot legislative election
Q3566196.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cyprus on 5 September 1976. The elections were contested by two alliances; one consisting of the Democratic Front (DIKO), the Progressive Party of Working People (AKEL) and the Movement for Social Democracy (EDEK) and one consisting of the Democratic National Party (DEK) and Democratic Rally (DISY).

Q4114548.label: 1996 Nigerien coup d'état
Q4114548.summary: The 1996 Nigerien coup d'état was a military coup d'état which occurred on 27 January 1996 in Niamey, Niger. It ousted Niger's first democratically elected president, Mahamane Ousmane after nearly three years in power and installed General Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara as head of state.

Q4870260.label: Battle of Alfambra
Q4870260.summary: The Battle of Alfambra took place near Alfambra from 5 to 8 February 1938, during the Spanish Civil War, and was a part of the Battle of Teruel. After the conquest of Teruel by the Republican army, the Nationalists started a counteroffensive in order to reocuppy Teruel. On 5 February, a huge Nationalist force broke the republican lines north of Teruel towards the Alfambra River, took 7,000 republican prisoners and threatened the Republican forces in Teruel.

Q7097460.label: Operation Retribution
Q7097460.summary: Operation Retribution was the Second World War air and naval blockade designed to prevent the seaborne evacuation of Axis forces from Tunisia to Sicily. Axis forces were isolated in northern Tunisia and faced Operation Vulcan, the final Allied assault. The equivalent blockade of air evacuation was Operation Flax.

Q3354740.label: Operation Kaika
Q3354740.summary: Operation Kaika was a joint operation between American Special Forces and Afghan National Army soldiers, to establish a control base as part of the larger Operation Mountain Thrust, and clear Taliban fighters from three villages about 12 miles southwest of Kandahar, Afghanistan in June 2006.

Q29034100.label: ISIL Daraa offensive (February 2017)
Q29034100.img: Free Syrian Army T-55 near Daraa.jpg
Q29034100.summary: The Southwestern Daraa offensive was launched by an Islamic State affiliate, the Khalid ibn al-Walid Army, in the southwest of Syria near the Golan Heights and on the border with Israel and Jordan.

Q227444.label: Zu Chongzhi
Q227444.img: 昆山亭林公园祖冲之像.jpg
Q227444.summary: Zu Chongzhi, courtesy name Wenyuan, was a Chinese astronomer, inventor, mathematician, politician, and writer during the Liu Song and Southern Qi dynasties. He was most notable for calculating pi as between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, a record in precision which would not be surpassed for nearly 900 years.

Q155764.label: Robert Brown
Q155764.desc: British botanist (1773-1858), discoverer of the cell nucleus and of Brownian Motion (1773–1858)
Q155764.summary: Robert Brown was a Scottish botanist and paleobotanist who made important contributions to botany largely through his pioneering use of the microscope. His contributions include one of the earliest detailed descriptions of the cell nucleus and cytoplasmic streaming; the observation of Brownian motion; early work on plant pollination and fertilisation, including being the first to recognise the fundamental difference between gymnosperms and angiosperms; and some of the earliest studies in palynology.

Q1409652.label: William Fothergill Cooke
Q1409652.summary: Sir William Fothergill Cooke was an English inventor. He was, with Charles Wheatstone, the co-inventor of the Cooke-Wheatstone electrical telegraph, which was patented in May 1837. Together with John Ricardo he founded the Electric Telegraph Company, the world's first public telegraph company, in 1846. He was knighted in 1869.

Citizenship: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

Q177268.label: moon of Mars
Q177268.summary: The two moons of Mars are Phobos and Deimos. They are irregular in shape. Both were discovered by American astronomer Asaph Hall in August 1877 and are named after the Greek mythological twin characters Phobos and Deimos who accompanied their father Ares into battle.

Q210036.label: Chechen Republic of Ichkeria
Q210036.desc: government in exile of Chechnya since 2000. Based in London
Q210036.summary: The Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, known simply as Ichkeria and colloquially as Chechnya, was a de facto state in the North Caucasus region. It controlled most of the former Checheno-Ingush ASSR from 1991 to 2000 and has been a government-in-exile since.
